1.d4 d5 2.c4 dxc4 3.e3 Nf6 4.Bxc4.strategy: Takes back the c4-pawn with the bishop, which lands on its best diagonal, while the centre stays intact. Black has no central pawn to disturb it, so White emerges with comfortable development and a small, lasting space advantage.

1.d4 d5 2.c4 dxc4 3.e3 Nf6 4.Bxc4 e6.strategy: Opens the way for the f8-bishop and prepares to strike at d4 with the c-pawn. Solid, but the pawn on e6 shuts in the c8-bishop, which has to be rerouted to the long diagonal or settle for a modest square.
